name: Michael Novogratz
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Wikidata (2025); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2024)
forbes_bio: Mike Novogratz is the founder, CEO and majority shareholder of Galaxy Digital Holdings, a crypto investment firm that trades on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
He began his career at Goldman Sachs in 1989, where he spent a decade and became a partner while the firm was still privately held.
Novogratz went on to work at private equity firm Fortress Investment Group, becoming its president.
He first bought bitcoin in 2013, and has since invested in a range of startups and tokens within the cryptocurrency industry.
His most notorious failure was betting big on Luna, a token tied to stablecoin TerraUSD, which blew up in 2022. Novogratz had tattooed its logo on his arm.

name: Sam Hupert
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Sam Hupert cofounded medical imaging company Pro Medicus in 1983 with Anthony Hall, who he met at a wine-tasting function.
Hupert is a medical doctor but stopped practicing in 1984 to run the company, which started as a medical billing and administrative business.
Pro Medicus made its first foray into the American market in 2004 via a licensing deal with digital imaging business Agfa.
Today 90% of Pro Medicus' revenues are generated in North America.

name: Massimo Doris
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Massimo Doris is the CEO of Italian bank Banca Mediolanum, which was founded by his father Ennio (d. 2021) in 1982.
He became CEO in 2008, when his father stepped down from the top job; he first joined the family firm in 1996.
While at Mediolanum, he also worked as a sales assistant at UBS, Merrill Lynch and Credit Suisse until he joined Mediolanum full-time in 1999.

name: Maja Oeri
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Maja Oeri is a descendant of Fritz Hoffmann-La Roche, founder of Switzerland-based pharma behemoth Roche.
She is a controlling shareholder of Roche, with just over 7.5% of the voting equity of the company.
At least fifteen other members of her extended family own shares of Roche as a group with pooled voting rights.
Oeri, a patron of the arts who studied art history in college, serves as a vice chair on the board of the Museum of Modern Art in New York City.
forbes_facts: Together with her husband, Oeri launched the Laurenz Foundation, supporting the fine arts, in 1999. It's named after their first-born son, who died young.

name: Robert Sands
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Robert and Richard Sands' father, Marvin, founded a humble wine business in 1945 at age 21.
That small operation has mushroomed into a publicly-traded behemoth now called Constellation Brands, which generates nearly $10 billion in annual revenue.
Robert Sands, who joined the company in 1986 as general counsel, was CEO from 2007 until March 2019. He is now a non-management director.
The company is known for its relentless streak of acquisitions. Subsidiaries include Robert Mondavi wine and Svedka Vodka.
Constellation also holds the rights to Grupo Modelo's U.S. beer business, including its Modelo and Corona labels.
The family (including niece Abigail Bennett and nephew Zachary Stern) received $1.5 billion (pre-tax) of cash to give up its enhanced voting power in 2022.
forbes_facts: In 2018, Constellation Brands announced a $4 billion investment in Toronto-listed cannabis firm Canopy Growth, in exchange for a 38% stake.

name: Jane Lauder
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Jane Lauder, granddaughter of cosmetics legend Estée Lauder, is a former executive vice president and chief data officer at her family's company.
Lauder joined Estée Lauder in 1996, a year after graduating from Stanford University. She previously managed the company's Clinique and Origins brands.
Estée Lauder, which her grandmother cofounded in 1946, now has over 20 brands and revenues of $14 billion.
Jane stepped down as an executive vice president at Estée Lauder in 2024. She has served on its board of directors since 2009.
In 2018, she joined the board of Eventbrite, the ticketing and event technology company.
forbes_facts: Lauder's husband, Kevin Warsh, also a Stanford grad, was the youngest-ever appointee to the Federal Reserve Board.

name: Filiz Sahenk
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2006-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Filiz Sahenk is Turkey's wealthiest woman and manages the fashion and tourism components of family conglomerate Dogus Holding.
Brands that Dogus represents in Turkey include Gucci, Emporio Armani, Loro Piana, Informal and Tod's.
The family had controlled Garanti Bank, the cornerstone of its fortune, selling it last 10% to Spain's BBVA in 2017, bringing in $900 million.
Today, besides branded clothing and tourism, Dogus is active in real estate, media, financial services, construction, autos and restaurants.
Dogus' hotel portfolio includes the Astir Palace in Greece, the Capri Palace in Italy and Rome's Aldrovandi Villa Borghese.
forbes_facts: Filiz oversees a foundation established in the name of her father, Ayhen Sahenk. The founder of Dogus, he died of a heart attack in 2001.
Her older brother, Ferit Sahenk, CEO of Dogus Holding, and her mother, Deniz Sahenk, are also billionaires.

name: Li Wanqiang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Li Wanqiang is a cofounder of Chinese smartphone giant Xiaomi.
Li was once the company's senior vice president in charge of marketing and sales. He left in 2019, citing personal reasons.
Li previously worked at software firm Kingsoft with Xiaomi chairman Lei Jun.

name: Christopher Rokos
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: Chris Rokos is the founder of hedge fund firm Rokos Capital Management.
Rokos is a macro investor who trades currencies, interest rates and commodities, as well as equities.
Rokos founded his London-based firm in 2015 and it now manages some $12 billion and employs more than 200 people.
A founding partner of Brevan Howard Asset Management, Rokos left the hedge fund firm after having a falling out with his partner, Alan Howard.

name: Udo Tschira
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Udo Tschira is the son of Klaus Tschira, the software pioneer who cofounded SAP (Systems, Applications, Products) in 1972.
He and his brother Harald inherited their dad's stake in SAP when he died in 2015. Klaus retired from the company in 1998 and left its board in 2007.
His sons carry on the activities of the Klaus Tschira Foundation, which promotes learning in natural sciences, mathematics and computer science.
The foundation, one of Germany's largest philanthropies, has awarded more than $740 million in cash grants and in-kind donations.

name: Dragos Paval
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Dragos Paval and his brother, Adrian, own Dedeman, a leading Romanian construction materials and do-it-yourself home products retailer.
The $2 billion (sales) company's 57 stores stock some 60,000 products, ranging from tools and building supplies to furniture and appliances.
The brothers founded the business in 1992 with a single location in Bacau, Romania.
They also own shares of several publicly traded Romanian companies and a portfolio of real estate in Bucharest and the northern city of Cluj.

name: Nevaldo Rocha
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2012-2019); Hurun Global (2014-2020)
forbes_bio: Nevaldo Rocha is the architect behind Riachuelo, one of Brazil's largest retailers.
In 1947, Rocha opened a clothing store with his brother Newton in the northeastern Brazilian city of Natal.
His Grupo Guararapes bought the Riachuelo brand in 1979, which has since become the centerpiece of the business.
Under Rocha's direction, Grupo Guararapes transformed from a clothing manufacturer to a fashion designer, producer and distributor.
In August 2018, Rocha resigned as president of the board. His children still work at the company.
forbes_facts: The third generation of the family is getting involved in the family business. Nevaldo's granddaughter Marcella orchestrated deals with Versace and Karl Lagerfeld.
